lesson_title: Two Tariffs, One Graph: Which Is Cheaper?
hook_text: Your family might be on the wrong electricity plan. One graph exposes it.
clip_script: Now to the crossing. The two lines intersect at one point — trace it down to the horizontal axis: 300 kilowatt-hours. Trace it across: R600. This is the break-even point: the usage at which both options cost exactly the same. Why does break-even matter? Because it splits the graph into two decision zones. To the left of 300 units — low usage — Option A is cheaper: light users should not pay a R150 entrance fee for a discount they barely use. To the right, Option B dips below A, because the saving of 50 cents on every unit eventually outweighs the fixed charge.
visual_style: Two coloured lines racing across a dark graph, the crossing point pulsing, then the two zones flooding green on either side with 'A WINS' and 'B WINS' labels.
pacing: Quick hook, deliberate pause at the crossing, energetic zone reveal.
